title: Teaching
text: My teaching interests span foundational and advanced statistics. I connect statistical theory with real-world examples, helping students develop practical intuition alongside a rigorous theoretical foundation. My interests range from random variables, linear regression, analysis of variance, and experimental design to contemporary methods such as variational inference, Gaussian processes, and nonparametric spatial statistics. Alongside building a strong theoretical foundation, I emphasize reproducible, version-controlled programming and the ethical use of confidential and non-public data.

title: Teaching
text:
Instructor of record

STAT 302: Statistical Methods, Texas A&M University, Fall 2022.
I served as the instructor of record for an introductory statistics course with 43 students, covering probability distributions, point and interval estimation, and hypothesis testing. I also collaborated with instructors across STAT 302 sections to maintain consistent grading standards and develop common examinations.

title: Teaching
text:
Teaching assistant

STAT 638: Applied Bayesian Methods, Texas A&M University, Fall 2023.
As a teaching assistant, I helped convert multiple-choice examinations from an in-person format to Canvas, creating and carefully validating the online questions and answer choices. This transition streamlined assessment administration and established a reusable, consistent examination workflow.
STAT 641: Methods of Statistics I, Texas A&M University, Spring 2020.
During the COVID-19 transition, I helped move homework submission and examination grading to eCampus. The centralized workflow simplified access to course materials, reduced reliance on email, and provided students with a consistent process for submitting assignments and receiving feedback.

title: Anirban Chakraborty
text:
I am a postdoctoral scholar in the Department of Public Health Sciences at the Medical University of South Carolina, working with Dr. Souvik Seal. My current research is focused on developing statistically accurate methods for biomarker identification and dimension reduction in single-cell and spatial omics, with a focus on multi-sample analysis.
I received my Ph.D. in Statistics from Texas A&M University (2024), advised by Dr. Matthias Katzfuss.

Research interests

Biomarker discovery in single-cell and spatial omics.
Multi-sample spatial omics and spatially aware dimension reduction.
Scalable Gaussian processes and Bayesian computation.
Bayesian spatial nonparametric estimation.
